are_you_ok.title: Smoke impacts Front Range with record heat, cooler weather on the way
are_you_ok.summary: The National Weather Service office in Boulder issued a heat advisory covering the entire Front Range (the populous corridor along the eastern edge of the Rocky Mountains that includes Boulder and Denver), taking effect at noon on Sunday and continuing through Monday. As the advisory held, the region also contended with gusty storms and wildfire smoke, and Denver set a new daily high-temperature record for Aug. 3 on Monday afternoon. Forecasters pointed to relief on Tuesday, with temperatures easing to around 80 degrees.
are_you_ok.description: A Heat Advisory remains in effect, with gusty storms and wildfire smoke expected. Relief comes on Tuesday as temperatures drop to 80 degrees.

conversation_starters.title: Coloradans celebrate 150 years of statehood
conversation_starters.summary: Colorado marked the 150th anniversary of its statehood on Saturday, the anniversary of its 1876 admission to the Union. Celebrations were held across the state, including a mile-long table set for 5,280 guests — a number chosen to echo Denver's 'Mile High' elevation of 5,280 feet.
conversation_starters.description: Saturday marked Colorado's 150th birthday. It became a state on this date in 1876, and Coloradans celebrated with a number of events across the state.

you_should_know.summary: Aurora Police officer Matthew Neely was charged with second-degree murder and reckless manslaughter in the fatal shooting of Rajon Belt-Stubblefield, nearly a year after the incident. Aurora is a large city adjacent to Denver.

you_should_know.summary: As monsoon rains proved insufficient to end Colorado's drought, several more reservoirs announced boat ramp closures amid dropping water levels, and another fish salvage was announced — part of a broader pattern of shrinking water supplies across the state.
you_should_know.description: Monsoon rains have not been enough to end Colorado's drought, and several more areas have announced boat ramp closures as water levels in our reservoirs continue to drop.

you_should_know.title: Firearm background checks reached record levels in July, CBI says
you_should_know.summary: The Colorado Bureau of Investigation reported that firearm background checks reached record levels in July, driven by a surge in purchases ahead of Senate Bill 25-003, a state gun measure that took effect Aug. 1.
you_should_know.description: The surge came as firearm purchases increased before Senate Bill 25-003 took effect Aug. 1.
